\paragraph{Monte Carlo.} 200 samples, process and mismatch together,
\SI{37}{\celsius}, at the conditions above. Output offset at zero electrode current has
a mean of \SI{-1.08}{\milli\volt} and \(\sigma = \SI{8.91}{\milli\volt}\)
(Figure~\ref{fig:tiaab-mc-voff}, Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-offset}); against the
\(\pm\SI{5}{\milli\volt}\) limit entered on the test the yield is \SI{48.0}{\percent}
per channel and \SI{5.3}{\percent} over four. Loop gain at DC averages
\SI{78.65}{\decibel}, and every sample clears the \SI{45}{\degree} phase-margin limit,
the worst at \SI{64.7}{\degree} (Figure~\ref{fig:tiaab-mc-pm},
Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-stability}). Signal bandwidth averages \SI{8.84}{\kilo\hertz}
against a \SI{1}{\kilo\hertz} floor met on all 200 samples
(Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-bandwidth}). Input current noise integrated
\SIrange{0.1}{100}{\hertz} is \SI{341.5}{\pico\ampere} against the
\SI{2}{\nano\ampere} channel budget (Figure~\ref{fig:tiaab-mc-inoise},
Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-noise}); it is referred to the \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} tap and
scales inversely with the tap selected.
